methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort (50 patients, 60% recurrence at median 202 days). Uni- and multivariable logistic regression with adjustment for age, sex, BMI, comorbidities, tumor stage. Appropriate statistical methods but: small sample (n=50, 30 events) limits power; selection bias evident (only cCR patients selected); covariates deliberately restricted to reduce overfitting; wide confidence intervals in multivariate model.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort of esophageal cancer patients undergoing watchful waiting (organ-sparing approach) post-chemoradiation; clinically relevant for emerging treatment paradigm. Identified risk factors (adenocarcinoma, circumferential extent >50%, dysphagia/fatigue at restaging) enable patient stratification but lack OS correlation.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort follows STROBE reporting with detailed methods, baseline/tumor characteristics in tables, multivariate regression results with OR/CI. Comprehensive Limitations section acknowledges retrospective design, selection bias, underreporting of chemoradiotherapy toxicities, limited follow-up (2 years). No data availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies recurrence predictors in watchful waiting cohort; extends limited literature (SANO trial). Findings (adenocarcinoma worse, dysphagia/fatigue at restaging) are hypothesis-generating but not surprising. Incremental contribution given small cohort size.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear Introduction contextualizing watchful waiting for esophageal cancer, detailed Methods describing patient selection and statistical approach, Results presenting univariate and multivariate findings systematically, Discussion interpreting mechanisms and limitations appropriately. Well-organized manuscript.

key_strengths: Addresses emerging clinical question: predictors of recurrence in watchful waiting approach for esophageal cancer (organ-sparing paradigm gaining importance)
Identifies clinically actionable risk factors (adenocarcinoma, >50% circumferential involvement, symptom burden at restaging) enabling risk stratification
Comprehensive Limitations section explicitly acknowledges selection bias, small sample size, potential overfitting, and restricted follow-up
Appropriate statistical approach with adjustment for confounders and acknowledgment of wide confidence intervals
key_concerns: Very small sample size (n=50, 30 recurrence events) severely limits statistical power and generalizability; multivariate model vulnerable to overfitting despite attempts to restrict covariates
Selection bias: only patients achieving cCR and deemed candidates for watchful waiting included; physician judgment and patient preference not quantified, limiting inference to broader population
Short follow-up (2 years) may miss late recurrences; authors justify based on prior data but limits long-term outcome assessment
Post-hoc subgroup analyses without adjustment for multiple comparisons; hypothesis-generating nature limits conclusiveness
Inability to determine specific rationale for individual patient decisions (surgery vs watchful waiting) after cCR
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective identification of recurrence predictors in small watchful waiting cohort with appropriate statistical adjustment. However, severe sample size limitation, selection bias, and hypothesis-generating nature of findings restrict impact. Suitable for Tier 3 with major revisions: prospective multicenter validation and larger cohorts essential before clinical implementation of risk stratification.
